exercise.name: Elliptical
library_steps: Step onto the pedals, hold the moving handles and start striding.
Keep a steady pace where you breathe harder but can still talk.
Lower the resistance for the last few minutes before you stop.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing upright on the two pedals, hands on the moving handles. Picture 1: left foot forward and higher, left handle pulled back; picture 2: the other way round.

setup.target: Upright trunk, whole foot on each pedal.
On the moving handles, arms opposite to the legs.

muscles.emg: Elliptical needs more knee bend and higher quadriceps (vastus lateralis) demand than walking (S1).
muscles.role: Library primary 'cardio' has no mask; front thigh lit (library secondary).
Steady the ankle on the pedal.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Trunk leans forward onto the arms.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Takes the work off the legs (S1).

sources.citation: Burnfield JM, Shu Y, Buster T, Taylor A. Similarity of joint kinematics and muscle demands between elliptical training and walking: implications for practice. Phys Ther. 2010;90(2):289-305.
sources.what_it_gave: Elliptical vs walking: more knee flexion through the cycle and greater quadriceps (vastus lateralis) demand; gluteus and hamstrings similar or higher.

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
